_how_to_add: One entry per place. lat/lon place the pin; photos are files in assets/gallery/ (a large .webp about 1400 px and a -sm.webp thumbnail about 480 px). "wide": true shows a photo across the full width of the panel, uncropped. Add talks and conferences the same way, with kind "talk", and research visits with kind "visit". A place can also have one "video" (an MP4 in assets/media/ with a poster picture); it plays silently when the pin is hovered or the place is opened. The About page shows every place too, as a numbered pin on a map of the United States and a card: optional "place" is a short location for that card (else "where"), and optional "cover" names the photo it shows (else the first photo that is not wide). See docs/MAINTAINING.md (Gallery).

places.title: Visiting researcher at CNR IRPI
places.text: A research visit to CNR IRPI, where SM2RAIN was developed: improving how it estimates rainfall from satellite soil moisture, and working on drainage from drydowns (DfD), published in the Journal of Hydrology in 2018.

photos.caption: At my desk at CNR IRPI, with the SM2RAIN plan on the whiteboard.
The SM2RAIN whiteboard: global ASCAT data, calibration runs with AMSR2 soil moisture for 2012–2015, and drainage from drydowns (DfD).
Presenting my PhD work during the visit: estimating drainage rate from soil moisture drydowns, toward a self-calibrated SM2RAIN.
In the office, 16 January 2017.
Working by the office window in Perugia.

places.title: EGU General Assembly, 2017 and 2018
places.text: Drainage from drydowns at EGU two years running: in 2017 a poster toward a global map of drainage rate using satellite soil moisture as the only input, and in 2018 drainage rate estimated from satellite soil moisture drydowns.

photos.caption: My EGU 2017 poster, unrolled in the office in Perugia: toward a global map of drainage rate using satellite soil moisture data as the only input.
With colleagues at EGU 2018 in Vienna, 10 April 2018.

places.title: SMAPVEX22 field campaign
places.text: NASA’s SMAP validation experiment in the forests of the US Northeast: surface roughness, soil moisture, bulk density and vegetation, measured on the ground under the satellite.

photos.caption: Measuring surface roughness with a pinboard.
Three TDR sensors measuring soil moisture.
Measuring bulk density: dig out a ring of soil, dry it, and measure the volume of the hole.
Taking soil samples next to the sensors.
Measuring tree height with a laser rangefinder and hypsometer.
Vegetation measurements with the Michigan Tech Research Institute team.
A solar-powered station logging soil moisture through the campaign.
A barred owl watching us from a dead branch in Harvard Forest, 26 July 2022.
The field team.

places.title: Crop growth stages, field measurements
places.text: Following soybean and corn through the season, counting leaves and measuring plant height, vegetation water content and leaf area index.

photos.caption: Counting soybean leaves.
Measuring leaf area index with an LAI meter.
Sampling corn for plant height and vegetation water content.
Soybean at the end of the season.

places.title: Across Alaska’s tundra
places.text: After more than a year developing and validating a satellite soil moisture product for northern latitudes, more than 1,200 miles across the tundra it was built for.

photos.caption: Alaska, May 2023, in one word.
On the shore of Cook Inlet in Lake Clark National Park, with the bush plane behind us, 30 May 2023.
Spruce-topped sea stacks from the deck of the boat.
Above a valley of spruce, with snow still on the peaks.
Walking the shore at dusk, with snow on the mountains across the water.
Alaska, the Last Frontier.

places.text: Presenting AgroTrack at AGU’s Annual Meeting: finding when farms irrigate from thermal satellite data, the study I began when I joined NASA.
